message.content: In lions, one of the most well‑studied dominant traits is the **presence of the MC1R gene variant that leads to a darker (blackish) coat**. This allele masks the recessive alleles that would otherwise produce lighter or spotted coats, making it a classic example of dominance in felid pigmentation.
